key_insight: Interpretable stylistic features reveal consistent, quantifiable differences between human and LLM-generated text across genres, models, and decoding strategies, enabling explainable characterization of stylistic variation.
problem_solved: Bridges the gap between binary detection and understanding by systematically measuring and interpreting how writing style varies between humans and LLMs (and across models/decoding), making stylistic differences actionable and explainable.
method: Assemble a large, genre-balanced corpus of human-written text and LLM outputs from multiple models and decoding strategies.
Extract interpretable stylistic features (lexical, syntactic, discourse, surprisal/entropy metrics) and quantify differences using statistical analysis.
Visualize style spaces and train simple classifiers/attribution analyses to link specific features to models, genres, and decoding methods.
impact: Provides AI/ML practitioners with explainable diagnostics for model evaluation, detection, and safe deployment—helping tune decoders, audit outputs by genre, and design interpretable defenses against misuse.
visual_elements: Heatmap of feature differences (features × [human, models, decoding modes]) highlighting which features separate groups most strongly
Dimensionality-reduction scatter (UMAP/t-SNE) showing clusters of human vs. model outputs colored by genre and model
Bar chart of top interpretable features by importance for attribution/detection (with short feature descriptions)
Sankey or small-multiples showing how decoding strategies (e.g., greedy, temperature, top-k/p) shift stylistic signatures
paper_title: Interpretable Stylistic Variation in Human and LLM Writing Across Genres, Models, and Decoding Strategies
paper_authors: Swati Rallapalli, Shannon Gallagher, Ronald Yurko, Tyler Brooks, Chuck Loughin
